In the case of AV operations, where trips are of longer duration and without established norms, much remains unknown about how people might interact in the absence of an attendant. Compounding this, substantial literature has identified safety concerns, particularly among women, regarding personal security while on public transit. Future research to better understand social dynamics among AV passengers is acutely needed to inform the design and operation of shared mobility services to ensure use among a wide range of potential riders. • The potential of AV-only facilities. Dedicated (AV-only) special use lanes, roadways, or transitways are a possible way to leverage the full benefits of automated control while allowing full reuse of the existing roadway system. AV fleets can theoretically operate safely with narrower lanes and closer headways, all of which would allow more space- and cost-efficient infrastructure than traditional roadway design that accommodates human-controlled vehicles. AVs could traverse traditional roadways built for human control and then gain access to AV-only facilities for enhanced performance in much the same way that modern freeways optimize the operation of automobiles with better geometrics and minimum speed limits, which allows safe high-speed travel. AV-only facilities may allow safer, high-capacity, and less congested flow. 56 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 5 Detailed Phase III Research Results Subsequent editions in the AMD implementation report series address in substantial detail the Phase III research results. These reports describe the key issues, detailed findings of Phase III work, and insight gained through the following subject content: • Fundamentals of Multimodal Service in AMDs • Analytical Insights into AV Fleet On-Demand Transport Service • AV Fleet Operational Control Systems • Battery Charging Strategy and Infrastructure • Station/Curbfront Infrastructure • Application of a Systems Engineering Methodology for Analyzing Operations and Electrification of Multimodal Transportation in AMDs The subsequent editions not only discuss the Phase III research findings to date, but will also progressively integrate Phase IV AMD research findings of related subtopics as initial AMDs begin to be realized at scale.
